source.title: Unveiling Downstream Performance Scaling of LLMs: A Clustering-Based Perspective
source.authors: Cheng-Zhong Xu; Kaiyuan Chen; Xiao Li; Ke Shen; Cheng-Gang Li

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether small-model results can predict downstream performance at larger scale, using a clustering-based accuracy prediction method rather than measuring the original held-out pretraining-loss scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper derives its downstream accuracy formula from an assumed power law for answer loss, but does not report an empirical test of held-out pretraining cross-entropy scaling or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Its reported prediction errors and pilot observations about downstream accuracy are its own results; cited results about other studies are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study trains nine dense models (122M to 70B) and predicts the 70B model's downstream accuracy from the eight smaller ones. Its reported prediction errors, plus pilot results on loss-versus-accuracy mismatch, bear directly on V6. It does not measure held-out loss scaling or compute-optimal allocation.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but the reader's per-benchmark COD values were misread. The authors conclude that clustering items by difficulty, fitting per-cluster curves and mapping subset to full set gives 1.55% mean and 2.68% max error for a 70B dense model. That headline uses a Qwen2-72B anchor in the mapping; without it the mean is 2.65%. They also report 2.18% after continued pretraining and 3.11% mean for an MoE target. They argue that training loss is an unreliable proxy for downstream performance.
record.recipe_differences: The study clusters benchmark samples by difficulty and predicts downstream accuracy using cluster-wise compute curves and a subset-to-full-set mapping. It does not measure held-out pretraining loss or test compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports differences across benchmark sets, between dense-to-dense and dense-to-MoE prediction, and between standard pretraining and high-quality continued pretraining. It also reports that downstream performance at a given training loss differs with model size and learning-rate schedule.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 4: the downstream extrapolation formula strongly changes errors. Without the random-guess or ceiling terms, or with a direct power law, the BBH final error is 4.1–11.7% versus 0.47% for the full formula.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream-accuracy extrapolation is highly sensitive to the fitted functional form (the downstream analogue of V7).

fits_no_version.finding: Different difficulty clusters within one benchmark follow distinct accuracy–compute curves with different thresholds and ceilings (Fig. 1 right, BBH).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream scaling is heterogeneous across items within a benchmark, so a single curve per benchmark bends or misfits.

record.problems: The principal dense-model prediction uses one 70B target and eight smaller models from the same model family, with evaluation on eight benchmarks; no uncertainty estimates are reported. Continued-pretraining results include larger errors on some benchmarks. The pilot training-loss comparisons are described qualitatively, with numerical points only in figures.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 reports per-benchmark errors for the comparator methods and COD without mapping; Table 2 also reports individual MoE benchmark errors. These individual comparator and MoE values were omitted to retain the main COD benchmark results, aggregate comparisons, continued-pretraining results, and the pilot loss-performance findings within the row budget.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss sweep; loss power law is only assumed (Assumption 1).
Loss extrapolation is not tested. Only downstream accuracy is extrapolated.
No fixed-compute allocation study. Models use a fixed token-to-compute-per-token ratio.
No shape comparisons at fixed parameter count.
No other modalities. Continued pretraining is evaluated only for downstream prediction, not for loss power laws.
No test of loss-law exponents or allocation fits.
Only one dense target (70B) from one model family. Multiple-choice logit tasks and smaller targets are excluded or flagged as weaker.

missing.what: COD without the anchor: mean 2.65%, max 4.98%, AGIEval 4.98%, MATH 3.99%. Anchor effects on baselines are also reported.
Prediction errors under alternative extrapolation formulas (f1, f2, f3) for BBH, MATH and MMLU-pro.
Per-benchmark errors for the MoE target, e.g. MBPP 8.11%, BBH 5.29%, DROP 5.24%.
Final error under different clustering algorithms (mean FE 1.55–6.43%).

record.verdict_notes: Table 1's text extraction interleaves the COD (w/o mapping) and COD (Complete) rows. The reader assigned the w/o-mapping values to r1–r8. The correct Complete values (2.68, 0.79, 0.47, 1.97, 2.42, 1.64, 1.05, 1.39) match Table 3 and Table A3 and average to 1.55. There is only one dense target model and no uncertainty is reported. The external 72B anchor in the mapping step means the 70B prediction is not purely from small models.

versions.untested_parts: No empirical held-out pretraining-loss sweep over parameters, tokens, or compute.
The paper predicts downstream accuracy, not large-run held-out loss from small-run loss fits.
No fixed-compute sweep or estimate of the loss-minimising parameter/token allocation.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count and loss.
Continued pretraining is evaluated for downstream prediction, but the paper does not test whether the same held-out-loss power law holds across training regimes or modalities.
Tests prediction of downstream benchmark accuracy from smaller-model evaluations; does not test downstream performance prediction from pretraining loss as a general method.

Does not test setup-dependent loss-law exponents or compute-optimal allocation. It does report heterogeneity and bending in downstream accuracy curves, but those are not tests of the specified loss-scaling and allocation claims.
